title: How DNA Copies Itself
summary: How a cell copies its DNA: the double helix unzips, new letters pair A with T and G with C, and one molecule becomes two.

pages.section: Hook: every new cell needs a full copy
pages.say: Before one of your cells splits in two, it has to copy its whole DNA. In a human cell that is about 3 billion letters, copied in a few hours, almost without a mistake.

beats.action: drifts slowly in the teal medium, surface proteins turning

beats.object: a strand of DNA inside the cell
beats.action: camera dives from the cell surface down to the strand, scale bar counting down
turns slowly as its base pairs glow orange along its length

pages.section: Intuition: DNA is a twisted zipper
pages.say: DNA is two strands twisted around each other, like a zipper. Each tooth is a letter: A, T, G or C. A letter on one side always fits one partner on the other side.

beats.action: turns across the frame, two backbones winding around each other
glow one after another along the helix like zipper teeth
each gets a leader line naming A, T, G and C

pages.section: Mechanism: an enzyme unzips the helix
pages.say: Copying starts when an enzyme called helicase grabs the helix. It pulls the two strands apart, breaking the weak bonds between the letters. Now each strand is a single row of letters, waiting.

beats.action: drifts in from the left toward the end of the helix
locks onto the helix end with an orange flash
unzips from the left, the two strands peeling apart into a fork
float apart, their bare letters facing outward

pages.section: Example: A pairs with T, G pairs with C
pages.say: Loose letters drift in the cell. An A only fits a T, held by 2 hydrogen bonds. A G only fits a C, held by 3. So each old strand decides exactly which new letters join it.

beats.action: flies into place opposite a thymine and locks with an orange flash
light up as dashed glowing lines between A and T
snaps together and three dashed bonds glow between them
pair along both open strands one after another

pages.say: When the zipper reaches the end, one molecule has become two. Each new helix keeps one old strand and one new strand. Both are exact copies, one for each new cell.

beats.action: runs to the right end as the last new letters pair
drift apart side by side, each twisting on its own

beats.object: the new strand in each helix
beats.action: glows orange beside its old partner strand
keep turning as the camera pulls far back and holds
